proposals.impact: Convert intro-load sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, 2 sessions reached the quiz intro screen and 0 started the quiz. The furthest_step_distribution shows both sessions stalled at intro_load. Nothing downstream was triggered. Every quiz completion is a potential email subscriber and a warm lead for coaching, so this is the most costly zero in the data set.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is loading but not converting a single visitor into a starter. Without seeing the current copy, the most evidence-backed single-file fix is to rewrite the intro CTA text. The current text is almost certainly generic ("Find out your money personality" or similar), which does nothing to earn the click from someone who has already spent years earning well but quietly avoiding their bank statements. Replace it with copy that names the specific discomfort the ICP already feels before they arrive, so the button feels like relief rather than a task.

proposals.impact: Lift open rates on lower-performing automations by applying Money Vigilance subject line pattern
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation is opening at 66.67% against 12 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% against 16 sends. That is a 29-percentage-point gap. The subject lines or sender names in the Vigilance sequence are doing something the Worship sequence is not. Given that both automations serve people who completed the same quiz funnel (once it works), closing that gap on the Worship sequence is the highest-yield email edit available right now.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject lines from the Money Vigilance sequence emails and compare them structurally to the Money Worship sequence subject lines. The Vigilance lines are almost certainly more specific to a lived feeling ("You checked your balance at 11pm again, didn't you") whereas the Worship lines are probably aspirational-abstract. Rewrite the first email subject line in the Worship automation to mirror the Vigilance pattern: name a specific behaviour the Money Worship person recognises in themselves, with no promise attached.

proposals.observation: Three CI workflows failed on 14 September: Daily Blog Post (08:55), Weekly Monday Report (10:59), and Funnel-Hack Digest (15:15). There are zero commits in the last 24 hours and only 1 post in the content queue. The blog pipeline is the primary top-of-funnel asset for organic discovery. If the Daily Blog Post workflow stays broken, the queue empties in roughly 24 hours and organic content stops entirely. The Weekly Monday Report failure means Joel also lost his own performance visibility. Fix the blog workflow first — it is the one that feeds the funnel.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the daily-blog-post.yml workflow run logs to find the failure reason (most likely a missing secret, a changed API endpoint, or a Node version mismatch introduced by a dependency update that never got a commit because the workflow is the only writer). Add a concrete fix for whichever single line is throwing, and add a Slack or email notification step so future failures surface within the hour rather than sitting silent until Fred's next audit.
proposals.new_text:
# Add after the final step in the job, before the closing of the steps block:

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3
        with:
          server_address: smtp.gmail.com
          server_port: 465
          username: ${{ secrets.NOTIFY_EMAIL_USER }}
          password: ${{ secrets.NOTIFY_EMAIL_PASS }}
          subject: "WoW CI: daily-blog-post failed — ${{ github.run_id }}"
          to: joel@wayofwealth.co.uk
          from: Fred <fred@wayofwealth.co.uk>
          body: |
            The daily-blog-post workflow failed at ${{ github.run_started_at }}.
            Run: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
            Check the logs above for the root cause before the content queue empties.
